NDT software in Charlotte: what the local inspection market actually looks like

Charlotte is not an oil town, and that shapes what an NDT company here needs from its software. Inspection work around the Queen City is spread across power generation, pipelines, fabrication and industrial maintenance. Duke Energy is headquartered uptown, and its McGuire Nuclear Station on Lake Norman and Catawba Nuclear Station across the state line in York County, South Carolina, pull in outage crews every refuelling season. The Colonial and Plantation pipelines run through the region and feed the Paw Creek terminal cluster on the west side of town. EPRI runs its NDE Center in Charlotte, which gives the area an unusually deep bench of UT, phased array and eddy current specialists. Add the fabrication and machine shops of Gaston, Iredell and Cabarrus counties, the motorsports engineering around Mooresville and Concord, Siemens Energy's gas turbine operation, and the steady flow of structural steel for a city that has not stopped building, and you get a market with a lot of variety and not much predictability.

The typical Charlotte NDT contractor is a small or mid-sized crew that might be on a nuclear outage in spring, a pipeline tie-in in early summer and a fabrication shop's weld backlog by autumn. The regulators set the context: the NRC for anything inside a nuclear plant fence, North Carolina's radiation protection program for your radiography licence (the state is an NRC Agreement State), PHMSA rules that bind the pipeline operators you work for, and the North Carolina Department of Labor boiler safety bureau for pressure equipment. Your software has to keep all of that straight without a full-time administrator, and that is what this page is about.

ERP for NDT companies in Charlotte: the short answer

The Atlantis ERP solution is a fully customized ERP built for NDT and inspection companies, set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, whose founder Anoop Rayavarapu is an ASNT NDT Level III. It runs quotes, jobs, technicians, equipment, reports and invoices in one system, configured around how a Charlotte contractor actually works. It is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, and pricing is quote on request.

In practice that means one job record that carries the client PO, the site, the methods, the codes, the procedure, the assigned technicians and the serial numbers of the instruments that went out the door. When the report is approved, the hours and equipment on that job are already sitting there for the invoice. When a technician's certification lapses, the system tells you before the client's gate does. You stop typing the same job into a quote spreadsheet, a whiteboard, a Word report and an accounting package. Each piece is a separate app that you can switch on as you need it; the full list is on the ERP apps page. The sections below walk through the apps that matter most for Charlotte work, one at a time, and show how each one applies to the jobs you are already doing.

Technician certification tracking software for Charlotte nuclear and pipeline work

The Certificates app holds every technician's certifications by scheme, level and method, and computes status automatically as active, expiring soon (within 90 days), expired or revoked. For crews that move between nuclear outages and commercial work, that one view is what keeps badging clean and stops a technician being turned around at the gate.

Each record carries the scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), the level from trainee to Level III, the method, the certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, the industry sector, OJT hours, training hours, exam results and attachments. Utility-specific qualifications, such as performance demonstration qualifications for ultrasonic examination, can be recorded under the other scheme with their own expiry dates. Vision tests sit alongside: near vision at Jaeger J1 or J2, far vision, colour perception, contrast, the examiner, the clinic and the certificate file. The employee NDT profile adds radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry, which is exactly what an outage badging office asks for.

Daily checks create warning tasks 90 days before a certification or vision test expires, and you can configure email alerts with your own recipients, look-ahead days and resend interval. Timesheets also warn when a technician logs hours against a method their certificate no longer covers. The ERP records certifications; your written practice and your Level III still decide who is qualified. The software just makes sure nobody forgets a date.

Calibration management software for instruments that move between sites

Asset Management tracks every flaw detector, phased array unit, thickness gauge, yoke, probe and source-related item by serial number, with calibration frequency and status, and Team Assignments warns you when someone tries to send an out-of-calibration instrument to a job. That warning matters in Charlotte, where the same PAUT unit might go from a power plant to a fab shop in the same week.

For each instrument you record the equipment type, asset tag, firmware, accessories, assigned person, condition and lifecycle state: new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired or disposed. Calibration records hold the provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, whether the lab is accredited, the result (pass, fail or conditional) and the next due date. A separate calibration certificate register stores the lab accreditation number, the PDF and a valid, expiring or expired status, with expiry alerts. In the Purchase app, vendors can be typed as OEM, dealer or calibration lab, with the lab's accreditation number and expiry, and purchase lines link to a specific equipment serial so a recalibration invoice lands against the right instrument.

Issue and return runs through supervisor and manager approval, with condition recorded both ways, so a cracked probe wedge after an outage has a name and a date on it. Reservations prevent two jobs claiming the same unit, the maintenance log records probe replacements and firmware updates, and consumables like couplant, penetrant, developer and magnetic particles carry reorder levels with a low-stock flag.

Crew dispatch and scheduling software for the I-77 and I-85 corridors

Team Assignments turns every job into a dispatch record that moves from planned to dispatched to in field to submitted to closed, with site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates. It blocks double-booking of technicians and of equipment serial numbers, which is the scheduling mistake that costs Charlotte contractors the most when outage season overlaps with regular clients.

A Charlotte crew can easily be spread between Catawba in South Carolina, a fabricator in Statesville, a terminal at Paw Creek and a shop in the Greenville-Spartanburg area on the same day. The technician availability calendar shows who is assigned, on leave, in training, sick or unavailable, and overlaps are blocked rather than flagged after the fact. Time Off requests feed the same calendar, so an approved vacation actually removes someone from the dispatch pool. Each technician shows current assignment, utilisation percentage and next available date, and you can work in calendar, kanban or list views depending on whether you are the dispatcher or the owner looking at the week.

The Fleet app handles the trucks: vehicle purpose, whether the vehicle can carry radioactive sources, the transport licence number and expiry, and vehicle assignment to a project and driver with dates and mileage. For radiography crews running out of Charlotte that is one less binder to keep current, and it puts the source-carrying truck on the same job record as the crew using it.

NDT reporting software built for Charlotte's method mix

The NDT Reports app covers 17 report types, each with its own numbering sequence: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday and coating, and computed radiography. That range fits a market where one week is heat exchanger tubing and power piping and the next is structural welds on a new tower.

Method-specific fields are built in: UT with a probe calibration table; RT with source, technique, IQI type and placement; MT technique and particle type; PT method and developer; PAUT focal laws; UT thickness readings by direction; and weld or job lines with defect type and orientation, closing with an overall result of acceptable, not acceptable or acceptable with remarks. Reports reference the work order, request, WPS, contract, drawing numbers, procedure and standard.

Every report moves through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures and a field for the third-party or authorized inspector's name and signature, which is useful on boiler and pressure vessel work. Company templates are versioned and can be Excel, Word, PDF or HTML with your logo and header; if a utility or EPC insists on its own Excel form, fields are mapped to cells and filled automatically. The offline field app works inside turbine buildings and tank farms with no signal, stores drafts and photos locally, captures signatures on screen and syncs later. For a closer look at reporting on its own, see Digital Twin Reporting Software.

Procedure control that stands up to a utility audit

The Procedures app is a controlled register of your NDT procedures with document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard such as ASME Section V, acceptance criteria and either the procedure text or an uploaded file. Approved revisions are locked, and every revision keeps a snapshot, so an auditor can see exactly what a technician was working to on a given date.

Nuclear and utility clients around Charlotte audit their vendors' quality programs closely, and procedure control is usually the first place they look. The workflow runs draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejected and archived states, and records who prepared, reviewed and approved each revision and when. Rejections carry a reason. Approvers get email notifications and reminders when something is waiting on them, so a revised UT procedure does not sit in someone's inbox through an outage.

There is also an AI-assisted first draft: describe the method, material and standard and the system produces a starting draft, falling back to a built-in template if needed. It saves typing, nothing more. A Level III still reviews, edits and approves every procedure before it is published. Where your quality system needs nonconformance and corrective action tracking, NCR and CAPA workflows can be configured during implementation and linked back to the job and the procedure involved.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Charlotte contracts

Quotations carry the job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, with NDT service products flagged by method and category and a global discount where you need one. Clients accept and sign online, and the accepted quote converts to a sales order. Invoicing then picks up the job, the PO and the hours without re-entry.

Charlotte work mixes day-rate outage crews, per-weld fabrication pricing and call-out work for terminals, so the invoice has to show its working. The invoice header records the NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with subtotals for labour, equipment and consumables. Each line can carry a cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours. Timesheets feed billing directly, with work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), a billable flag and a rate multiplier for overtime and weekend outage shifts. Expenses such as per diems and hotel nights near a plant can be re-billed to the job.

The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, outstanding invoices, bills and expenses over a 12-month view. Taxes and payment terms are configured during implementation, and if you want to keep your accountant on QuickBooks or NetSuite, the open REST API connects the ERP to them, scoped per implementation.

Winning more Charlotte work: CRM and dashboards

The CRM records each lead's service line, source, NDT service type, industry sector, site country, and estimated technicians and days, and scores it from 0 to 100 as hot, warm, nurture or cold. That helps a small office decide whether to chase a utility bid, a pipeline spread or a fabricator's weekly call-out.

Leads import from CSV, AI-personalised email previews help you follow up without writing each message from scratch, and any lead can be enrolled in a drip sequence by service line. The Business Cards feature reads a photo of a card from a trade show or a local ASNT section meeting and creates a CRM lead in one click. Your website enquiry forms feed the same pipeline.

Dashboards pull the operational numbers onto one screen: equipment calibration due and overdue, certifications expiring and expired, and issued equipment that is overdue for return, next to the financial view. Most owners start their Monday there.

Implementing the Atlantis ERP in Charlotte

Implementation is done remotely by Atlantis NDT and scheduled around Eastern time working hours, so it fits between jobs rather than stopping them. The order below is how most rollouts run.

  1. Discovery call. We walk through your methods, clients, report formats and how you dispatch today.
  2. Data import. Technicians, certifications, vision tests, instruments, calibration dates, clients and open jobs are loaded from your existing spreadsheets.
  3. Configuration. Report templates, numbering, procedure register, quote and invoice layouts, alert recipients and any integrations are set up for your company.
  4. Pilot job. One real job runs end to end, quote to invoice, with your crew using the offline field app.
  5. Go live and support. The rest of the team moves over, and Atlantis stays on for questions and adjustments.

Anything that is not a built-in feature, such as a client-specific approval step or a custom KPI, is configured during implementation rather than promised off the shelf. If your technicians need structured learning between outages, the eLearning portal and the Practical NDT 3D simulator can be added, and Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training.

If you are a Charlotte NDT company running on spreadsheets, a generic accounting package and a lot of phone calls, the Atlantis ERP gives you one system shaped around inspection work. Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT software for a Charlotte inspection company?

The best fit is software that covers certifications, calibration, dispatch, reporting and invoicing in one place. The Atlantis ERP does that for NDT companies and is configured to your methods and clients during implementation.

Can it track CP-189 and utility-specific qualifications for nuclear work?

Yes. CP-189 is a built-in scheme, and utility-specific qualifications can be recorded under the other scheme with their own dates, attachments and expiry alerts.

Does the field app work inside plants with no signal?

Yes. The offline field app stores drafts and photos locally and syncs when the technician is back in coverage.

Is the Atlantis ERP suitable for small NDT companies?

Yes. You switch on only the apps you need, and the setup is scaled to a small crew. Pricing is quote on request.

Can it connect to our accounting software?

Yes. The open REST API integrates with QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation.

Does Atlantis calculate inspection intervals or corrosion rates?

No. The ERP manages your business and reports; it does not calculate inspection intervals or corrosion rates. Atlantis does offer API 510, 570 and 653 inspection services.

How do we get started?

Send us your current setup and we will walk you through a demo. Ask a question about the Atlantis ERP in Charlotte.
